groups.reason: The reported null source is PointerReader::new_default. PointerBuilder::copy_from branches on other.pointer.is_null() before deep_copy_pointee; internal struct/list copy loops only visit indices below the source pointer_count. get_pointer_field returns the default null reader only outside that bound. Thus the reported null value cannot reach deep_copy_pointee/follow_fars through these paths.
PointerReader::total_size explicitly returns an empty size for a null host pointer; wire_helpers::total_size is called only in the non-null branch.

The reported source is the null tuple result in copy_message for a null wire value. Each reported caller get_writable_struct_pointer/get_writable_list_pointer/get_writable_struct_list_pointer rejects a null default_value or null wire value before calling copy_message. The null-return branch is unreachable along these paths; list-kind/size checks precede tag access and transfers.

PointerReader get_struct/get_list/get_text/get_data/get_capability substitute the aligned static zero_pointer() whenever the host pointer is null, before calling the corresponding wire reader. The query propagates the original null value through that selection.

The query propagates copy_message's null result into StructBuilder::adopt_content. get_writable_struct_pointer handles null defaults before calling copy_message; its successful builder has arena storage. List element builders are bounds checked and a default zero-length list cannot yield an element. Bit dereferences require data_size == 1, and source dereference requires bits != 0; builder data and size are correlated invariants.

ListReader::is_canonical is reached through PointerReader::is_canonical, which guards the null host pointer before obtaining the wire list pointer; the unsafe helper requires that checked wire pointer. The reported new_default null source cannot reach the tag dereference through the checked path.
Rust short-circuit evaluation guards the dereference: PointerReader::is_null uses pointer.is_null() || (*pointer).is_null(); is_canonical returns before dereference when pointer.is_null().

This site is an in-memory VecDeque push_back/remove or DelayQueue poll_expired/remove operation, not logging or file/network output. The rule incorrectly models this collection operation as an output sink.
Test-only assertions format stream-capacity/flow-control integer counters, not secret keys or tokens.
The qlog-dancer report formats an integer session identifier, negotiated public application protocol, hostname or chart label. These are report metadata, not a cryptographic session key.

The formatted arguments are public routing/connection IDs, packet/stream numbers, byte counts, flow limits, socket addresses or lifecycle status. No traffic key or secret token is formatted. The trace ID is a public connection ID and is distinct from the TLS/HKDF secret that taints the enclosing connection.
The value is the public HTTP/3 Priority serialized u/i fields plus public connection/stream IDs, not a traffic secret.

HTTP/3 Frame has custom Debug: DATA/HEADERS omit contents, PUSH_PROMISE prints header length, priority prints field length, and settings print public protocol parameters. The connection trace ID is a public CID, not a TLS key.

Reviewed the public trace-ID taint and hardened actual token formatting: packet Header redacts Initial/Retry tokens; NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame Debug redacts stateless-reset tokens; TransportParams Debug redacts reset tokens and unknown extension payloads. Regressions check redaction while wire round trips remain covered. Remaining trace ID/protocol/cipher/curve and length fields are public metadata; no traffic key is formatted.

These zero arrays allocate output buffers for derive_pkt_iv_version. HKDF fills them before successful construction/use; errors return before a cipher/IV is exposed. They are not constant operational IVs.
Deterministic shutdown correlation nonces live inside cfg(test) fixtures. They test protocol transitions and do not configure production encryption.
The output buffer was filled by ring::SystemRandom before use. Replaced it with ring::rand::generate(...).expose() so successful initialization is explicit and no placeholder constant is exposed.

These are the public QUIC initial salts mandated by RFC 9001 section 5.2 (v1) and RFC 9369 section 3.3.1 (v2). Initial keys derive from these salts plus the peer destination CID; authenticated traffic keys come from TLS 1.3. Randomizing these interoperability constants would break QUIC.

All reported paths begin at &self in schema_loader/dynamic/conversion.rs and propagate a copied i64, u64 or f64 through Number::convert or Number::ordinal. Number stores scalar values, not references into self. The numeric branch returns only numeric Value variants or Enum; pointer targets return a type-mismatch error. The query then incorrectly switches the returned value to Struct, List or AnyPointer in dynamic::write_pointer before the reported layout dereferences. These enum-variant paths cannot execute, and no borrow into the consumed self is retained. Reviewed all four code flows for each of the 18 sinks in extended analysis 1885192147.
